name: Triangulum Galaxy
tagline: The quiet third spiral — the Local Group's shy member, rich in star nurseries.
history: Triangulum is the third-largest galaxy in our Local Group after Andromeda and the Milky Way, and may be a gravitational satellite of Andromeda itself. Under dark skies it sits near the edge of naked-eye visibility — the most remote object some observers ever see. It is smaller and more orderly than its giant neighbors, with an unusually high rate of star formation: its H II region NGC 604 is one of the largest known stellar nurseries, over 1,500 light-years across and ionized by hundreds of massive young stars. Lacking a dominant central bulge, it is also a natural laboratory for testing dark-matter models.
